questions.question: What job does Chat request lifecycle (SSE) do for the rest of the system?
variants: Why does the rest of the system need Chat request lifecycle (SSE)?
What would a user notice first if Chat request lifecycle (SSE) stopped working?
questions.reference_answer: It POST /api/chat streams a persona-driven Claude reply through pre-checks, retrieval, sentence capping, post-checks and persistence.

orientation.purpose: Handles each chat message: it streams the persona's Claude reply to the browser as it is generated, running safety checks before and after, and saves the exchange.
orientation.decision: One async FastAPI endpoint streams Server-Sent Events from the async Anthropic client. A cheap Haiku hostile pre-check runs first, then retrieval and model choice, then a hard sentence cap. Guardrail and follow-up calls run concurrently after the stream. WebSockets, a blocking request and a worker queue were not chosen; the goals were low latency and a free event loop.

orientation.shaped_by: Yusuf Pisan wrote the first streaming version alone [human] in May 2026, reworked it with an AI co-author [assisted] in June, and hardened it alone [human] in July.

questions.question: What job does Persona prompt and retrieval modes do for the rest of the system?
variants: Why does the rest of the system need Persona prompt and retrieval modes?
What would a user notice first if Persona prompt and retrieval modes stopped working?
questions.reference_answer: It builds the system prompt from persona markdown files and tone controls, and selects context via six retrieval modes.

orientation.purpose: Builds the system prompt from the persona markdown files and tone settings, and chooses how much persona context each request gets.
orientation.decision: Persona knowledge is plain markdown in the repo, so it stays editable through git. Six retrieval modes are selectable at runtime: full, distilled, TF-IDF, Voyage embeddings, Haiku router and cascading. Cascading is the default, and a DB setting overrides env, which overrides the code default. Fine-tuning, one fixed full prompt and a vector DB service were not chosen; the full persona costs about 40K tokens per call.
orientation.shaped_by: Yusuf Pisan added the persona files alone [human] in May 2026, then built the retrieval modes and the June refactor with an AI co-author [assisted].

questions.question: What job does SQLite persistence (analytics.db) and backup do for the rest of the system?
variants: Why does the rest of the system need SQLite persistence (analytics.db) and backup?
What would a user notice first if SQLite persistence (analytics.db) and backup stopped working?
questions.reference_answer: It one SQLite DB on the Render persistent disk stores conversations, users and roles, bans, feedback, proposals, usage and settings.

orientation.purpose: One SQLite DB on the Render persistent disk stores conversations, users and roles, bans, feedback, proposals, usage and settings.
orientation.decision: Single-file SQLite with migrations in code (analytics.py, about 1.9K lines) is the system of record. Chat context is rebuilt from it by session_id. A daily gzip snapshot goes to a private GitHub repo via the Contents API. Not chosen: Postgres; managed DB; the browser or cookies for session state. Why: Simple and cheap for one owner; survives redeploys on a persistent disk. The backup guards against disk loss.
orientation.shaped_by: From its history: Yusuf Pisan [human].

questions.question: What job does Safety: hostile pre-check, guardrails, bans do for the rest of the system?
variants: Why does the rest of the system need Safety: hostile pre-check, guardrails, bans?
What would a user notice first if Safety: hostile pre-check, guardrails, bans stopped working?
questions.reference_answer: It classifies each message and post-checks each reply, with persistent strikes and bans.

orientation.purpose: Classifies each message and post-checks each reply, with persistent strikes and bans.
orientation.decision: Haiku pre-check (hostile, manipulation, abusive) with 3-strike or 24h bans keyed by stable visitor identity and persisted to SQLite. A Haiku post-check fails closed. The sentence limit is enforced server-side. Not chosen: Prompt-only guardrails; IP-based bans; third-party moderation. Why: Prompt-only rules were evaded; bans must survive redeploys and IP changes. Fingerprinting was explicitly rejected for privacy.
orientation.shaped_by: From its history: Yusuf Pisan [assisted], Yusuf Pisan [human].

questions.question: What job does Auth and role-based access do for the rest of the system?
variants: Why does the rest of the system need Auth and role-based access?
What would a user notice first if Auth and role-based access stopped working?
questions.reference_answer: It optional Google sign-in issues a JWT. Stackable roles map to capabilities that gate admin endpoints.

orientation.purpose: Provides optional Google sign-in and roles, so that only users with the right capabilities can reach admin endpoints.
orientation.decision: A Google ID token is exchanged for a JWT. The browser keeps the JWT in localStorage and sends it in the Authorization header, with no cookies, because the Netlify frontend and Render backend are on different origins. Roles live in SQLite and are resolved on every request so changes apply at once. Cookie sessions, an external auth provider and a fixed admin list were not chosen.
orientation.shaped_by: Yusuf Pisan wrote it alone [human], starting in May 2026 and continuing through the June and July commits.

questions.question: What job does Cost controls, rate limits and usage metering do for the rest of the system?
variants: Why does the rest of the system need Cost controls, rate limits and usage metering?
What would a user notice first if Cost controls, rate limits and usage metering stopped working?
questions.reference_answer: It layered limits and metering keep Claude spend bounded.

orientation.purpose: Keeps Claude API spend bounded on a public bot that runs on the owner's personal key, using limits and usage metering.
orientation.decision: Layered controls: per-minute and per-session rate limits, daily exchange caps, token and monthly dollar caps with a login-required threshold, and a bring-your-own-key exemption. Haiku side calls are metered through a context-local tracker. No limits, a paid-only gate and a flat quota were not chosen; the history only says the changes were cost-driven.

where.what: rate-limit and cap checks in endpoints

orientation.shaped_by: Yusuf Pisan built it across three commits from May to June 2026, all with an AI co-author [assisted], including disabling an unmetered daily cron.

variants: Why does the rest of the system need FAQ cache and voice replies?

questions.reference_answer: It pre-generated FAQ answers are matched by TF-IDF and served without a full LLM call. Cached answers can have ElevenLabs audio.

orientation.purpose: Pre-generated FAQ answers are matched by TF-IDF and served without a full LLM call. Cached answers can have ElevenLabs audio.
orientation.decision: Stale-while-revalidate FAQ entries keyed by persona_hash, generated on the distilled persona. Audio clips are stored on disk by a content hash of the answer. Not chosen: Regenerate the whole bank on each deploy; a manifest or DB column for audio. Why: A redeploy regeneration cost about $5. The content hash orphans old clips automatically.
orientation.shaped_by: From its history: Yusuf Pisan [assisted], Yusuf Pisan [human].

questions.question: What job does Admin dashboard and Persona Fixes loop do for the rest of the system?
variants: Why does the rest of the system need Admin dashboard and Persona Fixes loop?
What would a user notice first if Admin dashboard and Persona Fixes loop stopped working?
questions.reference_answer: It admins review conversations and rate replies. A background worker proposes persona edits, which become a GitHub PR.

orientation.purpose: Lets admins review conversations and rate replies, then turns that feedback into proposed persona edits delivered as a GitHub pull request.
orientation.decision: Feedback goes to Sonnet, which returns full-file rewrites. A background daemon thread does the work while the client polls, because synchronous generation timed out at the edge proxy. Edits are limited to an allowlist of persona files and open a PR rather than pushing to main, so a human approves. Manual edits and a job queue were not chosen.

where.what: admin dashboard tabs and polling UI
persona-fix generation and GitHub PR creation

orientation.shaped_by: Yusuf Pisan introduced it in May 2026 with an AI co-author [assisted], then extended the admin page and sessions alone [human] in late May and June.

variants: Why does the rest of the system need Content pipeline and CI/deploy?

questions.reference_answer: It headlines are scored and drafted into posts, which open a PR. Merge ingests them and CI gates deployment to Render.

orientation.purpose: Headlines are scored and drafted into posts, which open a PR. Merge ingests them and CI gates deployment to Render.
orientation.decision: Git is the approval and ingestion mechanism: a GitHub Action or local CLI drafts a post PR, and merge triggers a gated Render deploy. The CLI backend avoids API cost. CI gates on ruff, mypy, tests and build. Not chosen: A CMS; direct publishing; a manual deploy. Why: Reuses PR review and keeps humans in control. The cron was disabled to stop unmetered API spend.
orientation.shaped_by: From its history: YPai pipeline [human], Yusuf Pisan [human], Yusuf Pisan [assisted].

orientation.purpose: Resend handles inbound webhook mail, approval-gated draft replies, and notification emails.
orientation.decision: Inbound mail is stored in threads. Drafts are generated only on admin click and sent only after explicit approval. The notifier emails capability holders and throttles API-key alerts via a DB timestamp. Not chosen: Auto-reply; Gmail API; SMTP. Why: Prevents spam and cost, and gives a human gate. The features are inert without env config.
orientation.shaped_by: From its history: Yusuf Pisan [human].

variants: Why does the rest of the system need Contacts database with privacy filter?
What would a user notice first if Contacts database with privacy filter stopped working?
questions.reference_answer: It on-demand lookup in a separate contacts.db, injected transiently into prompts.

orientation.purpose: On-demand lookup in a separate contacts.db, injected transiently into prompts.
orientation.decision: A separate SQLite DB is built offline from email and LinkedIn data by scripts. A privacy filter excludes personal-email and family contacts. It is deployed to the Render disk. Not chosen: Put contacts in persona files; no contact lookup. Why: The data is large (about 18K entries) and private, so it is kept out of the prompt and out of git.
orientation.shaped_by: From its history: Yusuf Pisan [assisted].
